SMTO-EXE-0103 — The Gateway is already busy with other screen requests

GUID: 815eea6c-4c40-541f-8d5e-aa6df1276cab
Slug: screen-busy
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The computer SMTO was asked to look at was already handling four screen requests, so it turned this one away. Nothing was captured for it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether other tasks are looking at the same computer's screen right now, and give them a moment to finish. Each Gateway handles at most four screen requests at once, and all four were in use.
  2. If one of those tasks is no longer needed, open it and select Stop. Stopping a task frees the screen request it was using.
  3. Ask SMTO again for the screenshot or screen text. Nothing was captured the first time, so asking again once a slot is free is safe.

What success looks like

  • The new request finishes and the task shows the screenshot or screen text.

If it still fails

  • If it still says busy when no other tasks are using that computer, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't restart the Gateway while other tasks are still using it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway screen service rejected the request because four screen operations were already active, its per-Gateway concurrency limit.

What this means

  • The Gateway already had four active screen operations when another request arrived. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway already had four active screen operations when another request arrived.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect active screen requests and their owners before deciding whether one should be cancelled.

How to fix it

  • ScreenService.execute admits at most four concurrent screen operations per Gateway. Check which runs are currently calling screen.* on that Gateway, let them complete or cancel unneeded ones (task Stop sends /screen/cancel), then issue a new invocation.
  • Wait for one of the four active screen operations to finish or cancel it before making a new request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Wait for one of the four active screen operations to finish or cancel it before making a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Capacity is released by completed or deliberately cancelled work and the new explicit request is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
